purpose: Read-only check of bootstrap-head diversity before interpreting the weak short-run mean-policy score
method: Hash-check the own verified bundle, reload BootstrapQ with five heads and prior scale 1, reconstruct each original four-frame stack with initial-frame padding, infer learned/prior/total values in batches of 32 and compare their argmax actions. The canonical greedy-mean network must reproduce all recorded actions. Report raw-action agreement and within-head standard deviation across the 20 action values; verify the weights hash again afterward.
limitations: One selected 140-point stage-1 replay from the 16,384-action smoke checkpoint; not representative of the continuing fresh production learner or its training distribution.
Raw action disagreement is not necessarily behavioral disagreement: some key combinations have equivalent effects in a stage.
No individual-head game outcomes were measured. This is not evidence that any individual head plays better than the ensemble mean, or that disagreement caused its low score.

Removing the prior only for an action-agreement calculation is not a trained ablation or a performance evaluation. Learned and prior components interact; neither component's standalone argmax measures its contribution to score.

No replay actions, frames, head choices or diagnostic labels were fed into training. No policy, prior scale or evaluation rule was changed. The longer independent trial continues to its original complete-game evaluation gate.
